newsitem.title: IRAN: Hardline Iranian cleric warns Germany over charges.
newsitem.headline: Hardline Iranian cleric warns Germany over charges.

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric said on Friday Iranians would not tolerate German charges that Tehran leaders had ordered political killings in Germany.

"The (Iranian) people are ready to see themselves wounded and shot at but they are not ready to tolerate any insult to their sanctities," Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast live on state-run Tehran radio.

He was referring to charges by a German prosecutor that Iran's spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran leaders ordered the 1992 shootings of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin.
"Well, you saw Salman Rushdie's fate after that insult and rudeness," Jannati said.

Rushdie, a British novelist, has lived in hiding since 1989 when Iran's late spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini ordered his killing for allegedly blaspheming Islam in his novel "The Satanic Verses".

"We shall strongly insist on our positions and values and will not surrender to any judge or court," Jannati, a senior cleric known for his fiery rhetoric, told worshippers gathered at Tehran University.
President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and other Iranian government officials have been trying to ease tensions with Germany, Iran's main trade partner.
Iran's official news agency IRNA said on Thursday Rafsanjani had answered a recent message by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl. It did not give details.
Kohl told Rafsanjani in his letter that German courts were independent from the government and he was concerned about a deterioration in Bonn's relations with Tehran.
